patches.value: Twice differentiating u·u=1 in time gives 2|u_t|²+2u·u_tt=0. For an arbitrary coordinate j0∈{1,...,n}, twice differentiating in x_{j0} similarly gives 2|∂_{x_{j0}}u|²+2u·∂_{x_{j0}x_{j0}}u=0. Thus u·u_tt=−|u_t|² and u·∂_{x_{j0}x_{j0}}u=−|∂_{x_{j0}}u|². Generalize j0 over the spatial coordinates. Dot the normality equation for a with u and use |u|²=1. Finite distributivity and the definition of Δ_xu give a=u·(u_tt−Δ_xu)=Σ_{j=1}^n|∂_{x_j}u|²−|u_t|². The same calculation applies to every scalar satisfying that pointwise equation.
